name: IC-7000
subtitle: Field reference
kicker: Independent reference. Not an Icom publication and not affiliated with Icom.
verified: Compiled from the Icom IC-7000 Instruction Manual and published specifications, September 2026. Not checked against a radio. The reset procedures could not be read and are left out.
specs: 160 through 10 m, plus 6 m, 2 m and 70 cm
USB, LSB, CW, RTTY, AM, FM. WFM receive only. No D-STAR
2 to 100 W on HF and 6 m, 2 to 50 W on 2 m, 2 to 35 W on 70 cm
13.8 V DC plus or minus 15 per cent
1.3 A standby, 1.6 A at full audio
None. An external AH-4 or AT-180 is the option
Remote jack only. There is no USB port on this radio
keys: Short push cycles the menus within a group, M-1 to M-3. Hold about a second to change group.
Soft keys. What they do depends on the menu showing above them.
None of these keys exist on this radio. Everything goes through MENU and the soft keys.
Main dial, tuning step, and mode.
One concentric control doing all three.
External tuner, or the call channel.
ANF, MNF, NB, NR, P.AMP / ATT
Auto notch and recorder, manual notch, blanker, noise reduction, preamp and attenuator.
quick: RF power, mic gain, SSB transmit bandwidth
Also keyer speed, CW pitch, sidetone level, the twin peak filter, and the RTTY settings.
Quick split, split offset and lock
Also the repeater offset per band, one touch repeater, auto repeater, tuner settings, and the CI-V address, baud and transceive.
Contrast through to the power-on check.
filters: Wide, mid or narrow, with separate low and high edges, in quick set mode.
tasks: Hold the memory write key about a second to write the displayed frequency and mode into the shown channel.
The split soft key in the first menu row. Hold it about a second for quick split, once the offset is set in miscellaneous set mode.
RF power in quick set mode.

In FM, the shift soft key in the third menu row selects the direction, or off. Hold it for one touch repeater. The tone soft key selects encoder, tone squelch or digital squelch; hold to set the frequency or code.
control: The remote jack on the rear. There is no USB port
300 up to 19200, or auto. Auto is the default
A CT-17 or equivalent is required. With no USB port there is no way around it
notes: No USB port. A level converter is not an accessory on this radio, it is the only way a computer talks to it.
No internal tuner, and two antenna sockets. The same two things to check as the IC-7100.
Twenty-two amps at full output from a radio small enough to take anywhere is the trap. Fuse and wire for the current, not the size.
The detachable head is a connector, and connectors fail. Carry the spare cable.
This radio is out of production. Spares and heads come from the used market, which is a reason to write your settings down below.
settings: CI-V address, as read from set mode
